question: In pre-independent India, who was the first person to discuss the concept of poverty line?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dadabhai Naoroji.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji** was the first person to discuss the **concept of poverty line** in pre-independent India.
 
• He introduced the concept in his book **"Poverty and Un-British Rule in India" **published in **1901.**
 
• Naoroji defined poverty line as the **minimum income required** to meet the basic needs of an individual.
 
• He argued that poverty was not due to the **laziness or incompetence** of the Indian people but was a result of the **economic policies** of the British rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahadev Govind Ranade** was a **social reformer and scholar** who advocated for the **upliftment of women and lower castes.**
 
• **B.R. Ambedkar** was a prominent leader of the **Dalit community** and played a key role in **drafting the Indian constitution.**
 
• **M.K. Gandhi** was a leader of the **Indian independence movement** and is known for his **nonviolent civil disobedience tactics.**
